title: RunuX: Deterministic Fixed-Point Attention, Isometric PolarQuant KV-Compression, and Grid-Carbon Adaptive Scheduling — Scientific Benchmarking & Soak Dataset
description: Open scientific replication dataset, empirical telemetry, and academic paper accompanying the RunuX AI Runtime. Includes: (1) Local physical open-weights Mistral 7B Instruct v0.2 benchmarks on NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU, eliminating the 8k+ token CUDA Out-Of-Memory (OOM) failure cliff and enabling full 32k context in only 4.88 GB VRAM (preserving 9.68 GB headroom), (2) 1-Hour continuous hardware soak telemetry on Tesla T4 (3.10 TFLOPS sustained, 76.0°C thermal equilibrium, 0.000 MB VRAM leakage across 10.26M passes and 10.51B tokens), (3) Google Cloud TPU v5e/v6e Trillium Spot Serverless preemption resilience protocol (< 12 ms checkpointing, zero token loss, 2.32x throughput speedup via MLGO systolic tiling), (4) Mistral Large 2 (128k context) PolarQuant 3-bit KV-cache reduction (4.92x), (5) INT64 bit-exact zero-drift attention proofs (Delta_num = 0.000), (6) 1-Bit SignSGD Megatron-LM 70B communication reduction (32.0x), (7) $50 GCP Spot/Serverless economic reproducibility schedule, and (8) Open-science collaboration and partnership framework for Mistral AI, NVIDIA, and Google Cloud. Note: Closed-source RunuX runtime engine source code, compiled micro-kernel binaries, and private cryptographic salts remain proprietary under pending patent protection at INPI.
